comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Thank you for watching and exploring Fogo Island with us! 🌋❤ If you lived here, would you return after a volcanic eruption or choose to start over somewhere safer? I'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments! 👇

comments.author: @prof.tarekeldomiaty5069
comments.text: Wish Fogo citizens were asked the question of what makes them live in volcanic Island?

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That's a great point. Hearing that answer directly from people who were born and raised on Fogo would add even more depth to the story. From what we explored, family ties, fertile volcanic soil, livelihoods, and a deep attachment to home are all part of why people stay. Thanks for raising this! 🇨🇻🙏

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: Absolutely fascinating! The courage of people living alongside an active volcano is truly inspiring. This documentary beautifully shows the powerful connection between people and the land they call home. What an incredible story!

replies.author: @its_Lenettesantos
replies.text: Why don’t you get real clips instead of clipping random people and things

replies.author: @BestHiddenPlaces
replies.text: Glad you found it fascinating! It really is an incredible story of resilience and connection to the land.

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: Imagine rebuilding your home on the same land where a volcano once destroyed everything. The resilience of Fogo's people is incredible! Would you have the courage to return?

comments.author: @EarthUnknown66
comments.text: I really love your videos, I guess I need to learn a lot more from your channel.

comments.author: @earthwaystravel
comments.text: Tourism brings jobs and opportunities to Fogo, but could too many visitors eventually threaten the peaceful island lifestyle that makes this place so special? 🌋👇

comments.author: @raymondcooper7658
comments.text: Fogo’s volcanic landscape is incredible, but would you risk living near an active volcano to stay on the land your family has called home for generations? 🌋👇

comments.author: @WorldLivingTravel8
comments.text: Rebuilding stone houses inside an active caldera just because volcanic soil makes world  class wine is mind blowing. The everyday courage of people on Fogo is unreal

comments.author: @TravelThePlanet68
comments.text: What fascinates me most about Fogo is that people are not just living near an active volcano. They have built an entire way of life around it. Would you ever choose to live here?
